title: Tempo prefill hysteresis and attention-skein: reduce microburst tails with lookahead kernel-fit
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a prefill admission hysteresis layer (Tempo) combined with an attention-skein smoothing model to reduce tail latency during microbursts. Tempo applies a short, configurable hold-and-merge window for very short prefill bursts to assemble higher-quality batches without violating per-request latency SLOs. Attention-skein smooths KV and attention memory spikes by staggering attention-heavy requests across kernels and suggesting lookahead kernel-fits before decode starts.
motivation: In recent production traces we've observed frequent 99.9th percentile spikes caused by microbursts of short prefill-heavy requests and attention-context churn. These spikes increase token cost (because of suboptimal kernel selection) and break tight latency SLOs for premium customers. Existing admission gates are too eager and kernel-fit decisions happen only at decode time, causing expensive kernel switches mid-decode.
accepted_risks: Slight increases to median latency for very short requests if the hysteresis window holds them for batching; must be carefully gated per-customer SLA. Kernel lookahead may slightly increase CPU for profiling during prefill but should be bounded by sampling rate.
design_summary: Tempo is a short-term admission buffer with three modes: pass-through (default for high-priority tokens), opportunistic-hold (for short prefill bursts where adding up to N additional requests reduces overall per-token cost), and adaptive-hold (uses recent stream history to adapt the hold time). Attention-skein models request attention footprint (KV size and per-layer attention cost) and assigns a priority score. Before decode, the scheduler consults a lookahead module that samples light-weight kernel latency/throughput profiles and assigns a preferred kernel variant; if the chosen kernel is unavailable, requests are routed to the nearest acceptable kernel variant with graceful degradation.
acceptance_criteria: 99.9th percentile end-to-end latency reduced by >= 20% on synthetic microburst workload compared to baseline
Average per-token GPU cost reduced by >= 7% for the burst workload after kernel-fit routing enabled
No customer-facing errors introduced and all existing unit/integration tests pass
Feature toggle to fully disable Tempo and attention-skein at runtime
Rolling deploy plan validated in staging with canary traffic and rollback hooks
implementation_notes: Implement Tempo as a pluggable admission policy in admission-controller v2 (configurable hold_ms, max_batch_increase, per-tenant exemptions)
Add attention-skein estimator in prefill path: lightweight per-request per-layer KV estimator based on seq_len, prompt type, and model hints
Lookahead kernel-fit: sample microbenchmarks on live or recent telemetry to score kernel variants; cache scores per-model/seqlen range
Decode scheduler changes: allow kernel preference hint to be attached to request context and respected by decode-orchestrator; add fallback rules for kernel unavailability
Telemetry: emit metrics for hold window utilization, additional wait time distribution, kernel-fit mismatches, and per-request attention footprint
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: RFC drafted by Aisha; initial call with runtime and infra teams. Chosen approach: admission hysteresis + lookahead kernel hints.
2026-03-03: Prototype Tempo admission buffer implemented in a sidecar for local experiment; synthetic microburst tests show 18% 99.9p reduction with hold_ms=12 and max_batch_increase=3.
2026-03-05: Attention-skein estimator spec completed; Marcelo implemented estimator prototype (Python) and integrated it into prefill simulator.
2026-03-07: Kernel lookahead sampler implemented; small-run profiling shows consistent preference for quantized kernel variant for short-seq requests on A100s.
2026-03-08: Merged staging branch for Tempo buffer and attention estimator behind feature flags; running canary job against conv-load test harness
open_questions: What per-customer default should we use for hold_ms? (current experiments show 8-20ms sweet spot)
Should large-tenant burst exemptions default to enabled to avoid added tail for some latency-sensitive customers?
What sampling rate for lookahead profiling balances accuracy vs overhead? (current test: 1%)
rollout_plan: Alpha: Enable Tempo+attention-skein for internal staging with synthetic burst suite (1 day)
Canary: 1% traffic on runtime-1.22 cluster, monitor 50/95/99/99.9 latency and kernel-mismatch metrics (3 days)
Gradual ramp: increase to 25% with adaptive hold disabled for P0 customers; enable adaptive-hold for non-P0 after validating cost savings (7 days)
Full: global rollout with per-tenant config and automatic rollback if 99.9p worsens beyond threshold
test_plan: Unit tests for hysteresis logic and hold edge cases
End-to-end simulation with synthetic microbursts of varying shapes and customer mixes
A/B comparison in staging using production traces replay
Chaos test: simulate kernel unavailability and verify graceful fallback rules
Performance regression tests to ensure median latency overhead < 5ms for non-burst traffic
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboard: Tempo hold usage, average extra wait_ms, batch size delta distribution
Alerts: spike in 99.9p latency > baseline + 15% during canary
Alerts: kernel-fit mismatch rate > 2% over 5 minutes
Audit logs: per-request kernel preference and final kernel used (for debugging)
comments: Leah Kim (PM) 2026-03-02: Strong preference to make hold_ms tenant-configurable. Please add safe defaults and an escape hatch for enterprise SLAs.
Omar N'Diaye (Infra) 2026-03-04: Concern about increased memory churn when combining multiple attention-heavy requests; proposer to add a soft cap on simultaneously admitted attention footprint.
Marcus Lee (SRE) 2026-03-06: Suggest we bind the lookahead sampler to the same runtime node to avoid cross-node profiling noise.
Design review 2026-03-07: Reviewed UI for tenant controls in Console; action: PM to add a simple toggle and three presets (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive).
